title: To Thee, My God, My Days Are Known
description: To Thee, My God, My Days Are Known in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 616 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"My times are in thy hand."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: To Thee, my God, my days are known; My soul en-joys the thought; My ac-tions all be-fore thy face, Nor are my faults for-got.

lines: To Thee, my God, my days are known;
My actions all before thy face,
And all my walks of daily life
Each golden hour of beaming light
Full in thy view through life I pass,
And in thy view I die;
And when each mortal bond is broke,
Shall find my God is nigh.

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
